sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Rock Canyon High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Rock Canyon High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Rock Canyon High School basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
What makes a game clip suitable for a shot tracer?

Choose a continuous shot with the ball and basket visible. Include the pass or final dribble, the release and the finish. If players block the ball, inspect the preview carefully or choose a clearer attempt.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Sequoia High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Sequoia High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Montgomery Bell Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Montgomery Bell Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Montgomery Bell Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for St. John'S Prep In Danvers basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your St. John'S Prep In Danvers basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Gilmour Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Gilmour Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Gilmour Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your St James Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for St James Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your St James Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Burlingame High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Burlingame High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for James Clemens High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your James Clemens High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Greens Farms Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Greens Farms Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Greens Farms Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Western Reserve Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Western Reserve Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Western Reserve Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Lake Zurich High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Lake Zurich High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Dickinson High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Dickinson High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Dme Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Dme Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Dme Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Governor'S Academy Massachusetts basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Governor'S Academy Massachusetts basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Alta Loma High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Alta Loma High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Alta Loma High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your North Raleigh Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for North Raleigh Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your North Raleigh Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your St Peter'S Prep Jersey City basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for St Peter'S Prep Jersey City basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your St Peter'S Prep Jersey City basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Auburn Riverside High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Auburn Riverside High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Auburn Riverside High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your South Elgin High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for South Elgin High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your South Elgin High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Madison Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Madison Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Madison Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Holy Names Academy Seattle basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Holy Names Academy Seattle basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Holy Names Academy Seattle basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your The Governor'S Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for The Governor'S Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your The Governor'S Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Kalani High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Kalani High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for La Jolla High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your La Jolla High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Saint Thomas Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Saint Thomas Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Saint Thomas Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Calvary Christian Academy Fort Lauderdale basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Calvary Christian Academy Fort Lauderdale basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Calvary Christian Academy Fort Lauderdale basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow

subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Clovis West High School basketball highlight

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together

sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Clovis West High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Ballantyne Ridge High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Ballantyne Ridge High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Ballantyne Ridge High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Virginia Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Virginia Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Virginia Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Virginia Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Tri Cities High School basketball highlight

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together

sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Tri Cities High School basketball clip with a tracer

subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Atrisco Heritage Academy Hs basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Atrisco Heritage Academy Hs basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Atrisco Heritage Academy Hs basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Christ Presbyterian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Christ Presbyterian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Christ Presbyterian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Glynn Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Glynn Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Glynn Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Holy Names Academy Washington basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Holy Names Academy Washington basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Holy Names Academy Washington basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Mckinney Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Mckinney Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Mckinney Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.

subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.
