sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Parnassus Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Parnassus Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Parnassus Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Perris High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Perris High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Cottage Hill Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Cottage Hill Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Cottage Hill Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Haddonfield Memorial High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Haddonfield Memorial High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Haddonfield Memorial High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Mundy'S Mill High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Mundy'S Mill High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Mundy'S Mill High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Liberty Pines Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Liberty Pines Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Liberty Pines Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Liberty Pines Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Southwest Florida Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Southwest Florida Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Southwest Florida Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Round Rock Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Round Rock Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Round Rock Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Round Rock Christian Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Sacred Heart Prep Atherton basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Sacred Heart Prep Atherton basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Sacred Heart Prep Atherton basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand

sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Owego Free Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Owego Free Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Walpole High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Walpole High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Maui Prep Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Maui Prep Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Maui Prep Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Vallivue High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Vallivue High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Vallivue High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Spartanburg Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Spartanburg Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Spartanburg Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Spartanburg Christian Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Huitt Bethany Oklahoma School District basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Huitt Bethany Oklahoma School District basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Huitt Bethany Oklahoma School District basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your East Catholic High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for East Catholic High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your East Catholic High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.

Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Westmoreland High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Westmoreland High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Westmoreland High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Mt St Dominic Academy Caldwell basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Mt St Dominic Academy Caldwell basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Northridge Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Northridge Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Northridge Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Schenectady High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Schenectady High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Hazelwood East High School basketball highlight

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together

sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Hazelwood East High School basketball clip with a tracer

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Cathedral Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Cathedral Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Cathedral Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Cathedral Prep basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.
Is the demo a Cathedral Prep basketball video?
The demo is a shared HoopCut basketball example. It lets you see the effect before uploading your own clip. HoopCut is an independent editing tool.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Hudson'S Bay High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Hudson'S Bay High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Hudson'S Bay High School basketball clip with a tracer

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Hawthorne Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Hawthorne Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Hawthorne Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Hawthorne Christian Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.

Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Cedar Stars Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Cedar Stars Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Cedar Stars Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Cedar Stars Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.

Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

description: Make your Brophy Prep basketball shot stand out. Upload a practice or game clip, preview a tracer and export a highlight with HoopCut.
heading: Brophy Prep basketball highlights — add a shot tracer
intro: Turn your Brophy Prep basketball recording into a highlight worth sharing. Pick a jumper from practice or a game, upload your clip and add a visible trail that follows the ball toward the hoop.
heroDetail: Start with one clear attempt: the shooter, ball and basket in frame. Select up to 30 seconds and preview the trail before exporting.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Brophy Prep basketball clip
workflowHeading: From practice recording to a shareable shot
sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Brophy Prep basketball highlights
examplesHeading: Watch the ball trail in action

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Brophy Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Brophy Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Brophy Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Boston Trinity Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Boston Trinity Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Boston Trinity Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Gfi Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Gfi Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Gfi Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Academy Montgomery Al Sports basketball highlight

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Academy Montgomery Al Sports basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Madison Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Madison Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your West Deptford High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for West Deptford High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your West Deptford High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Titusville High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Titusville High School basketball clip with a tracer

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.
